tvOS multi-layer parallax poster

I wanted to know if one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas could tilt three separate drawable HTML layers as a tvOS poster card, cast soft parallax shadows between them, sweep a glossy squircle sheen across the face and keep tilted controls clickable with updateElementGeometry().

Show the code 3-layer markup, 3D uMvp projection, inter-layer shadow shader, ElementGL uploads and 2D fallback
  1. Three independent drawable poster layers. Background artwork (depth 0), midground emblem and pills (depth 1), and foreground editable title and action buttons (depth 2) live inside one <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree>.
  2. Per-layer 3D perspective uMvp and hit-test matrix. Maps each layer at z = k * splitWorld through shared yaw/pitch rotation and camera projection, returning both clip-space uMvp and projective DOMMatrix.
  3. Squircle mask, inter-layer shadows and diagonal specular sheen. Clips corners to a continuous squircle SDF, samples blurred upper-layer alpha opposite the pointer light, and sweeps a glossy specular highlight across the card.
  4. Single ElementGL context, premultiplied uploads and geometry sync. Sets UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL = true, gates uploads on hasPainted inside paint, calls stage.begin() before stage.upload(), and updates updateElementGeometry() scaled by geometryUnit().
  5. Five-argument drawElementImage() 2D fallback and plain-HTML rescue. Renders affine parallax layers with 2D cast shadows when WebGL 2 is absent, and moves the three layers into #plain-host on context loss.

How it works

  • Each poster layer lives in its own 268 × 376 CSS pixel drawable container inside #tv-canvas. Only #poster-title-input and the two action buttons on #tv-layer-fg accept pointer events; #tv-layer-bg and #tv-layer-mid stay non-interactive so background layers never intercept taps aimed at the floating controls.
  • ElementGL owns the page's single WebGL 2 context. Inside the paint handler, I call stage.begin() first and then upload only whichever layers changed via stage.upload(layer) with UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL set to true. Pointer drags and auto-tilt animate at 60 fps by updating matrices and uniforms without re-uploading DOM textures.
  • To cast real parallax drop shadows, Pass 1 (#tv-layer-bg) binds #tv-layer-mid on texture unit 1 and #tv-layer-fg on texture unit 2, blurring their alpha masks at UV offsets opposite the pointer light. Pass 2 (#tv-layer-mid) binds #tv-layer-fg on unit 1 so the title and buttons cast a sharper shadow onto the midground emblem strip.
  • syncHitGeometry() passes each layer's 3D projective DOMMatrix scaled by geometryUnit() to canvas.updateElementGeometry() and flips dataset.hitTick whenever the transform changes so Chromium's hit-test cache stays aligned with the tilted card.

Live checks

Each check builds its own isolated fixture on testStage() and retires its canvas when finished, leaving the poster above untouched.

ResultExperimentDetail

Findings

Measured in headless Google Chrome 160.0.8188.0 canary on 2026-11-27 at 412 px and 2.625 DPR (SwiftShader WebGL). Chrome 159 on Android and npm run check:jank stay not verified.

  • Works: multi-layer texElementSubImage2D() with inter-layer cast shadows. Binding the midground texture on texture unit 1 and foreground texture on texture unit 2 lets the shader blur upper alpha masks at UV offsets opposite the pointer light in one ElementGL context (1.09 MP, 8.68 MB, 0 GL errors).
  • Works: Z-separation drives real parallax travel. Tilting rightward with Split layers raised from 0 px to 36 px shifts the foreground marker relative to the background centre from -0.1 px to +21.0 px, while pointer tilt from (-1, -1) to (+1, +1) sweeps corner specular luminance from 111/23 to 23/112.
  • Works: tilted controls stay clickable and editable. Scaling each layer's projective DOMMatrix by geometryUnit() and toggling dataset.hitTick keeps Play trailer, + Watchlist and #poster-title-input responsive to real pointer clicks at tilted angles.
  • Not verified on mobile hardware: touch dragging, glossy frame rate, and soft keyboard behaviour on #poster-title-input in Chrome 159 for Android at 412 px and 2.625 DPR.
